title: Time
description: Dates, zones, and durations with time.h
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## time.h

`gmtime_r`, `strftime`, and `difftime` for deterministic UTC output.

exercises.title: Build a UTC instant
exercises.description: Create January 1, 2024, 12:00:00 UTC with `time.h::Utc` and print it.

exercises.title: Components in Tokyo
exercises.description: Use `time.h_tz::Asia::Tokyo` and `with_ymd_and_hms` for 2023-03-15 14:30:00. Print year, month name, day, hour, minute, weekday (same labels as the Go exercise).
exercises.expected_output:
Year: 2023
Month: March
Day: 15
Hour: 14
Minute: 30
Weekday: Wednesday

exercises.title: Durations
exercises.description: Build a duration of 2 hours + 30 minutes and print it in Go-style `HhMmMs` (`2h30m0s`). Then print `500ms` for a half-second (format these two lines exactly).

exercises.title: Parse naive datetime
exercises.description: Parse `"2024-06-15 09:30:00"` with format `'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'`, interpret as UTC with `.and_utc()`, print the `DateTime<Utc>`.

exercises.title: Format
exercises.description: July 4, 2024 16:00 UTC. Print `MM/DD/YYYY` on the first line, then a long line like `Thursday, July 4, 2024` (match the sample exactly).

exercises.title: Add duration
exercises.description: Start at 2024-01-15 10:00 UTC. Add 3 days and 5 hours; print the result.

exercises.title: Subtract instants
exercises.description: Fixed `now` = 2024-12-25 UTC midnight, `then` = 2024-11-25 UTC midnight. Print the duration in Go-style hours (`720h0m0s`) then `Days: 30`.

exercises.title: Before / after
exercises.description: Compare Jan 1 2024 and Dec 31 2024 UTC with `lt`/`gt` (or `<`/`>`) and print the two lines from the Go exercise.
exercises.expected_output:
January 1 is before December 31: true
December 31 is after January 1: true

exercises.title: Fixed clock (no wall time)
exercises.description: Go used `time.Now` + `Sleep`. Here: use `Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2024, 6, 1, 10, 15, 30)`. Print the instant, then hour and minute, then the instant plus one second (`+ Duration::seconds(1)`) labeled `After +1s:` — deterministic output.
